_about: DCM Warp HYBRID (GPU-resident per-step + host low-cadence remesh) vs the existing single-cell DCM per-step path. gbook RTX A5000, measured 2026-06-20. Single-cell icosphere subdiv=3 (642 nodes), physics = radial-shell turgor + cortex edge springs + overdamped Langevin, dt=1e-7.

config.physics: radial turgor (law2) + cortex harmonic edge springs + overdamped Langevin (device RNG)

node_pool_resync_validated_cpu: 162 -> 390 active nodes via 228 SPLIT ops across 19 remesh events; pool fixed-size (pos array never reallocated); loop stable, cell inflates 7.5->9.55 um
interpretation: The GPU-resident Warp per-step loop removes the existing per-step cpu_local_snapshot host sync -> 30x faster per step on the same A5000, same config. Remesh stays on host (dynamic topology, low cadence); the node-pool keeps the Warp pos array fixed-size so the GPU side is static-array. The host remesh epoch (~113ms: unoptimized python remesh_pass with per-op reclassify + full-pool re-upload) is the remaining lever and amortizes with cadence (10x at every-500-steps, 23.5x at every-2000). Even worst-case aggressive remesh stays 10x over the existing path.
